environment.accelerator: CPU (XGBoost and scikit-learn do not use the Apple GPU/MPS here)

evaluation_note: Acceptance criterion: XGBoost MAE below the 3-month moving average (app/ml/acceptance.py). It does NOT beat the 3-month moving average on MAE; this is reported as is.
deployment_label: Experimental: trained on ONE real UK person's account (MoneyVis); accuracy for other people is not established

datasets.name: MoneyVis Bank Transactions Dataset
datasets.publisher: Robert S. Laramee, University of Nottingham (Mendeley Data)
datasets.publication: Firat et al., MoneyVis: Open Bank Transaction Data for Visualization and Beyond, EuroVis 2023
datasets.population: ONE anonymised retail current account (names, account number and sort code replaced)

monthly.missing_month_treatment: a month with no spending rows counts as 0 spending (genuinely no activity on the account)

datasets.preprocessing: See app/ml/data/moneyvis.py: serial-date correction, spending/income definitions, partial months dropped.
datasets.missing_values: debit/credit blank means 0 for that side; 24 rows without a category are counted as spending
datasets.known_biases: One person, one UK bank, 2015-2022, GBP; includes mortgage, Amazon-heavy shopping.

methodology: XGBRegressor (existing hyperparameters), target = next month / trailing 6-month mean, 9 lag features.
limitations: A single person's history: about 70 usable months. It cannot show that the model works for other people. Category-level forecasts are not trained on real data and are not shown. Stage 2 (multi-person, Berka) is pending the data owner's permission.
reproducible: python -m app.ml.train forecast (seed 7) with the raw file above
